money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Sweden's official currency is the Swedish Krona (SEK). Some businesses no longer accept cash. Declare amounts over 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Sweden and any non-European Union (EU) country. This includes all forms of currency, not just cash. You'll be fined if you don't declare it or give the wrong information on entry or exit. You don't need to declare currency if you're travelling to or from another EU country.

laws.rule: Allemansrätten (the right of public access) is not a law of its own. It is set in the constitution (Regeringsformen 2 kap. 15 §) and bounded by other laws. The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (Naturvårdsverket) says it does not apply on private gardens or inside a house's home-peace zone (hemfridszon), where a visitor can be fined for trespass, and does not cover motor traffic or off-road driving. Picking may be banned in national parks and nature reserves; the Agency tells visitors to check local rules there. Camping on a public bathing place is usually set by the municipality's local public order rules, so check the municipality.

Dogs in nature: from 1 March to 20 August the law requires a dog owner to keep the dog under extra close watch, and the dog must not run loose; in most cases this means a lead. Naturvårdsverket adds that protected areas such as national parks and nature reserves often have a lead requirement, and municipalities can set lead rules or dog bans in built-up areas by local order.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Sweden is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Allemansrätten (the right of public access): you may roam, hike, cycle, swim, pick wild berries, flowers and mushrooms, and camp briefly, but don't disturb or destroy. Keep off cultivated land, gardens and the private zone near homes; take all litter home; don't damage living trees; no off-road driving; dogs on a leash 1 March to 20 August and always in reindeer areas. Check fire bans and protected-area rules.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

Transportstyrelsen (the transport agency) registers operators through its e-service Dronarsidan: for people aged 18 or over who are registered as living in Sweden, and organisations based in Sweden. Application fee SEK 190 and annual fee SEK 250.
Someone living in another EU/EEA state registers there, not in Sweden. People living outside the EU/EEA can apply on paper (form TSL7180), which takes longer.
LFV (the air navigation service) publishes the Dronarkartan drone map showing airports, airspace and restricted areas. Temporary NOTAM information must be checked separately.

Image Bank Sweden (run with Visit Sweden) offers logo-free images and videos for presenting Sweden abroad, free of charge once the terms are accepted; credit the creator. The page does not mention aerial footage, and the full terms text was not read. A search snippet says no registration is needed.
